The new Brawlers of Behemat boxed set is available to pre-order from Saturday, so we’re taking a look at just how two mighty Mega-Gargants smashing each other works.

Brawlers of Behemat is the game of monstrous melee and bone-crunching combat for two players. You’ll both shatter limbs, hurl buildings, and try to pummel your opponent into submission, and games can last around 15 minutes – perfect for play in a lunch break or as a warm up for a game of Warhammer Age of Sigmar.

The Mega-Gargants in the box can each be built as a Warstomper, Kraken-eater, or Gatebreaker, who have different attacks and abilities. They each start with the Clobber attack, and as they take more damage, they get angrier, which gives them access to even more devastating attacks.

CLOBBER

Randomise a body part on the other brawler and inflict D6 damage on it. Then, move the other brawler up to 1 stride in any direction.

When you make the Clobber attack, you randomly strike a body part of your opposing Mega-Gargant – head, torso, right arm, left arm, right leg, or left leg. Cause enough damage to the head, torso, or any two limbs, and your foe is taken down!

Each body part has a tracker so you know how badly damaged it is. When the damage token advances to a different colour (from white to green, or green to orange), your battle fury increases and you gain access to bigger, more powerful events. For example, the Warstomper can perform the Kicked in the Goolies attack! 

RIGHT LEG (5)

KICKED IN THE GOOLIES

Inflict D6 damage on the other brawler’s torso. If you inflicted more than 4 damage, advance the other brawler’s battle fury tracker down 1 box (i.e. from white to green or green to orange).

You might also notice the red skull shield – these are a reaction space. When the damage token reaches one of these, your Mega-Gargant can use the special ability on their dashboard – the Kraken-eater gets to use Netted and get access to some handy re-rolls.

NETTED

In this brawler’s next turn, when rolling to see how much damage an attack inflicts, you can re-roll any or all of the dice from that roll.

When a brawler takes sufficient damage, they each get access to Colossal Smash. This attack damages each body part of your opponent AND does even more damage as you knock them through a terrain piece.

COLOSSAL SMASH

Place the other brawler within 1 stride of your brawler. If you wish to place the other brawler in a space occupied by any buildings or barricades, remove them before placing the brawler. Then inflict D6 damage on each of the other brawler’s body parts, starting with the torso. For each barricade and building removed, you can add 2 to one of those D6 rolls (say whether you will do so before making the roll).

This fun, fast-paced game is also a great way to kick off a new Sons of Behemat army or easily add a pair of Mega-Gargants to an existing one. Rules for King Brodd and the Beast-smasher Mega-Gargant will also be in a future issue of White Dwarf.

Brawlers of Behemat is available to pre-order from Saturday, alongside the new Sons of Behemat battletome and miniatures, so you don’t have long to wait until you can duel in the ruins of Embergard.

For the last few years, Space Marines have been singling out targets for destruction with their Oath of Moment ability, but the new Codex brings a new army rule. Oath is dead, long live Combat Doctrines.

Veterans among you may remember Combat Doctrines from Codexes past (including the popular Gladius Task Force detachment from 10th edition), and like Mk VII helmets and back banners, they’ve been updated for a new age of warfare. This army rule reflects the ability of the Adeptus Astartes to rapidly shift their tactics in the face of evolving threats, adopting Tactical, Assault, and Devastator doctrines to grant their entire strike force a useful ability once per game.

ARMY RULES

COMBAT DOCTRINES
ASSAULT DOCTRINE

When this unit is selected to make an advance move, that advance move does not prevent this unit from being eligible to declare a charge. 

DEVASTATOR DOCTRINE

This unit’s ranged attacks have [ASSAULT].

TACTICAL DOCTRINE

When this unit is selected to make a fall-back move, that fall-back move does not prevent this unit from being eligible to shoot and eligible to declare a charge.

Unless otherwise stated:

  • You can only select each combat doctrine once per battle.

  • Only one combat doctrine can be active for each unit. If a rule makes a combat doctrine active for a unit, any combat doctrine previously active for that unit is no longer active for that unit.

Once per game might not seem like a lot, but Space Marines specialise in the application of overwhelming force at decisive moments, and one turn of shooting or charging after Advance moves can be the difference between bowling over your opponent’s gun line and sitting stranded in no-man’s-land.

Certain detachments also grant the ability to use doctrines more than once. Assault Brethren, Tactical Brethren, and Devastator Brethren all give you an extra use of their respective doctrine as their detachment ability – though the Unique: Doctrines tag means you’ll need to work out which is your favourite.

Space Marine Captains are a true force multiplier with their new ability to activate a doctrine of their choice for their unit, even if it’s different from the one everyone else is using. Coupled with their Transhuman Strategist ability, which gives you an extra Command Point in every battle round, you’ll want to make sure the boss is coming along whenever his Astartes deploy.

Despite Captains being able to activate doctrines at will, you can normally only have one active at a time, but some experienced units supersede that. Captains in the Tactical Brethren detachment can take an enhancement that puts them in Tactical doctrine at all times, in addition to any others, while Roboute Guilliman – who literally wrote the book on Space Marine warfare – has all three active. Always.

CODEX ADEPT

The assault doctrine, devastator doctrine and tactical doctrine are active for this unit.

Some Characters even have their abilities enhanced under specific doctrines. Salamanders Captain Adrax Agatone, for example, gives his unit the ability to re-roll wound rolls of 1 with Unto the Anvil, but these convert into full wound re-rolls while in the Assault doctrine. Likewise, Caanok Var normally has to choose if he gives his unit Sustained Hits 1: non-Monster/Vehicle or Lethal Hits: Monster/Vehicle, but in the Tactical doctrine he can just do both.

These new rules give Space Marines of all stripes far more agility than before, and helps to get them into the perfect position to launch powerful attacks with their newfound strength. Come back tomorrow to hear more about those detachments!

Armies of Renown are a great way to add some extra theming to your Warhammer Age of Sigmar armies and trade a little flexibility for fun and characterful rules. Today, we’re seeing what the Sons of Behemat have to offer.

The new gargant witch Ma Maegran can gather a gaggle of LITTLE* units into the Matriarch’s Mob – a roving entourage of attendants and true believers who hope to prove themselves and earn a blessing from the Chooser of the Mighty. Even those closest to her have no idea how far her powers truly flex, and many far-fetched stories that start with “I Heard She Can…” end up proving shockingly true.

MATRIARCH'S MOB

Once Per Turn (Army), Your Hero Phase

I’VE HEARD SHE CAN…

Ma Maegran's true abilities are shrouded in mystery, but rumours will always exist, and gargants are nothing if not susceptible to a good yarn.

Effect: Pick 1 of the following effects:

...Shoot Fire From Her Eyes!: Inflict D3 mortal damage on each visible enemy unit within 12" of the friendly Ma Maegran.

...Turn You Into a Human!: Pick a visible friendly unit wholly within 12" of the friendly Ma Maegran. Until the start of your next turn, enemy units have a maximum control score of 1 while they are in combat with that unit.

...Make Ya Big and Strong!: Pick another visible friendly unit wholly within 12" of the friendly Ma Maegran. Add 1 to the Attacks characteristic of that unit's weapons for the rest of the turn.

...Whiz the Biggest Bangers!: Add 1 to casting rolls for the friendly Ma Maegran until the start of your next turn.

Many of the battle traits, enhancements, and spells unique to this Army of Renown affect targets within 12” of Ma Maegran, so it works best as a close-knit wrecking ball that rumbles from one objective to the next. The witch is so vital to the game plan that many of her gargants will gladly throw themselves in front of harm, for fear of disappointing the Chooser and catching a curse that saps them of their strength. 

MATRIARCH'S MOB

Passive

DON’T LET NUFFIN’ HAPPEN TO HER!

Ma Maegran is a figure of veneration and no small amount of fear among gargantkind. Hoping to be made 'really, really big', most gargants will do everything they can to keep her alive.

Effect: While the friendly Ma Maegran is within the combat range of another friendly LITTLE unit:

  • She has WARD (5+).

  • Each time you make a successful ward roll for her, allocate 1 mortal damage to another friendly LITTLE unit within her combat range after the damage sequence for her has been resolved (ward rolls cannot be made for those damage points).

  • Ignore negative modifiers to hit rolls and wound rolls for that other friendly LITTLE unit's combat attacks.

The next Army of Renown, the Stomper Tribe,** also rewards keeping smaller gargants around a locus of power, though this time one of the towering Warstomper Mega-Gargants. With a name like that you can probably guess what their favourite activity is, and the battle trait Stomp! Stomp! Stomp! Stomp! is a very thematically appropriate way to pile mortal damage into your foes.

STOMPER TRIBE

Once Per Turn (Army), Any Combat Phase

STOMP! STOMP! STOMP! STOMP!

The Stomper Tribe are famous for one thing, and you'll never guess what it is...

Declare: Pick an enemy unit in combat with a friendly STOMPER TRIBE unit to be the target.

Effect: Roll a dice. Add 1 to the roll for each friendly STOMPER TRIBE model in combat with the target. On a 5+:

  • The target has STRIKE-LAST for the rest of the turn.

  • Inflict 3 mortal damage on the target.

Where the Matriarch’s Mob has loads of utility abilities that can heal friendly units, fortify their hides, or order them out of risky combats, the Stomper Tribe is all about killing squishy little mortals as much as you possibly can. The Gettin’ Stuck In ability is a flexible way to boost both your LITTLE horde and your BIG unit in combat, giving the melee weapons used by the former an extra point of Damage – upping their swings with their weapon to an impressive 3 Damage and their ‘Eadbutt to Damage 4 – while the latter’s melee weapons have more Rend to bust through pesky armour.

STOMPER TRIBE

Once Per Turn (Army), Any Combat Phase

GETTIN’ STUCK IN

Warstompers and their followers relish the visceral thrill of battle, wading in wherever the fighting is most bloody.

Declare: Pick a friendly STOMPER TRIBE unit in combat to be the target.

Effect: If the target is LITTLE, pick a model in the target unit. Add 1 to the Damage characteristic of that model's melee weapons for the rest of the turn.

If the target is BIG, add 1 to the Rend characteristic of its melee weapons for the rest of the turn.

In addition to these Armies of Renown, you also get five Regiments of Renown all based around legendary Sons of Behemat who’ve been known to work with factions across the Mortal Realms:

  • Odo Godswallow fights alongside DESTRUCTION armies – A Beast-smasher Mega-Gargant especially effective against Monsters.

  • Bundo Whalebiter works with ORDER and DESTRUCTION armies – A Kraken-eater Mega-Gargant smart enough to pull off a cunning trap.

  • One-eyed Grunnock battles with CHAOS and DESTRUCTION armies – A Warstomper Mega-Gargant who disrupts enemy attacks with seismic stomps.

  • Big Drogg Fort-Kicka accompanies DEATH and DESTRUCTION armies – A Gatebreaker Mega-Gargant with breath that can literally kill.

  • Krong the Club can be used by ANY army – A Mancrusher Gargant whose own body is a lethal crushing weapon.


Between them, you can field a Mega-Gargant in any army in the game, so if you ever feel the need for some extreme damage to back up your disciplined Ossiarch legions or reaving Idoneth Deepkin, there’s a Regiment of Renown for you.

From a ragtag band of surviving Guardsmen to a handful of specialist Space Marines, two upcoming novels from Black Library show the odds the beleaguered Imperium must overcome to ensure its survival.

Crucible of Fire

Author Tom R Pike’s first full length Black Library novel follows Astra Militarum Lieutenant Kallisto Rytsar* who, when his company is decimated, must lead a ragtag group of surviving tanks and their crews on a mission to secure a vital manufactorum. 

Unfortunately for Rytsar, they're not the only ones with their eyes on the complex, as a massive ork warband is on the way to loot it for themselves! With the xenos closing in, the Valhallan officer is forced to arm workers and the wounded in a desperate attempt to repel their attacks – can they hold out until reinforcements arrive?

Raptors: War and Shadow

Strike from shadow. Choose the place and time of battle. Seize victory by any means necessary. These are the doctrines that define the Raptors Chapter, doctrines which are put to the test under the most extreme circumstances in War and Shadow.

This new novel by William Crowe – whose previous credits include the Astra Militarum novel, Veterans of the Fall and various short stories – follows a demi-company led by Lieutenant Chandrel Voise, tasked with destroying a tendril of Hive Fleet Leviathan.

After arriving on an isolated world, with no hope of reinforcements or resupply, the unorthodox tactics of the Raptors are tested to the very limit as the hunters become the hunted. With every bolt round fired bringing the Space Marines closer to victory or defeat, the Lieutenant is left with a stark choice – save the world, or save the warriors under his command.

Crucible of Fire and Raptors: War and Shadow will both be available to pre-order soon. In the meantime, follow another rag-tag bunch of Astra Militarum troops in Demolisher and see how the Ultramarines fare against Hive Fleet Leviathan in Leviathan.

* As first seen in the short story Worm of Valhalla – available via the Black Library App.

Gargants are pretty handy at smashing things to a pulp, but that doesn’t make them simple brutes. Some are good at throwing things, or weaving powerful spells, and today we’re going to find out what the newcomers can do.

Ma Maegran

As an old and powerful witch among a people with little magical aptitude, Ma Maegran commands nervous respect from even the Mega-Gargants that tower over her, and it’s not without reason. Rumours that she can bless her allies with untold strength and stature are completely true, and if a BIG* unit from your army is slain, a LITTLE comrade may just take their place.

MA MAEGRAN

CHOOSER OF THE MIGHTY

Once Per Battle, Any Movement Phase

CHOOSER OF THE MIGHTY

Eyes aglow with strange and forbidding light, Maegran draws upon her mightiest gifts: the ability to bestow bigness, either spiritual or physical, on a worthy gargant.

Declare: Pick another visible friendly LITTLE unit wholly within 12" of this unit to be mighty.

Effect: Pick 1 of the following effects:

  • For the rest of the turn, each time you make an unmodified wound roll of 6 for a combat attack made by the mighty unit, inflict 1 mortal damage on the target of the attack after the FIGHT ability has been resolved.

  • Pick a point on the battlefield within 1" of the mighty unit, then pick a friendly non-UNIQUE BIG unit that has been destroyed to be the target. Set up a replacement unit identical to the target within l" of that point, then allocate 10 damage points to it (ward rolls cannot be made for those damage points). The replacement unit can only be set up in combat with units that the mighty unit was in combat with when it was picked to be mighty. Then, 1 model in the mighty unit is slain.

For all her magical power though – including the new Lore of Behemat – Ma Maegran is not a standout fighter among her kin, and shepherds a pair of Ancient Ghyrochs to help keep particularly nasty foes off her back. These ornery beasts are infused with the life-giving power of Ghyran and regenerate wounds at an astonishing rate, giving them plenty of time to gore whatever’s in front of them.

And gore they do, with a chunky melee profile that can increase its Damage characteristic to 4 by combining their Charge ability and some bellowed ‘encouragement’ from Ma Maegran.

Mega-Gargants

Speaking of damage, Mega-Gargants have learned that there are two ways to swing a club after all – down, and sideways. Unfortunately for the teeming masses that swarm around them, this means that they can now choose between Calamitous Sweep and Crushing Blow profiles for their main attacks, trading raw force for a wider area of effect. This gives these devastating creatures a more reliable damage output, making it easier for you to smash stuff up.**

The immense weapons wielded by Mega-Gargants can be brought down for an obliteratingly heavy strike or swept through enemy ranks like a battering ram.

The other big change to Mega-Gargants is a reduction to their Health characteristic. There are two main reasons for this. It better reflects the size of the miniatures, bringing them in line with similar Monsters. Secondly, it means that each one will be lower in points, so you’ll be able to unleash more Mega-Gargants, making it easier to contest multiple objectives and complete more battle tactics.

Rock-hurlers

Smaller gargants get plenty of battlefield skills to play around with too. The new Rock-hurlers have developed some shockingly advanced battlefield tactics by gargant standards – rather than throwing boulders as hard as they can, they’ve learned to just drop them on nearby foes or roll them across the ground for better accuracy.

ROCK-HURLERS

These gargants have learnt that if you hurl your rock in specific ways, more enemies go 'squish' - and it's funnier to boot.

Drop: This unit's ranged weapons have Shoot in Combat and this unit can use the 'Covering Fire' command even if it is in combat.

Toss: Add 6" to the Range characteristic of this unit's ranged weapons.

Roll: Add 1 to hit rolls for this unit's shooting attacks.

Mancrusher Gargants

Mancrusher Gargants, meanwhile, surrender to an all-too-familiar vice: the approval of their mates. In typical loutish fashion, they constantly egg each other on, always coming up with violent escapades that their towering comrades would never dare do. That such dares tend to involve people being crushed with clubs is a moot point.

MANCRUSHER GARGANT

Once Per Battle (Army), Deployment Phase

BET YOU CAN’T…

Mancrushers are often egged on - or just straight up bullied - into various escapades by their mates.

Declare: Pick each friendly Mancrusher Gargant on the battlefield to be the targets.

Effect: Pick 1 of the following effects:

... Kill the Big 'Eads!: For the rest of the battle, add 1 to the Attacks characteristic of each target's melee weapons while they are in combat with any enemy HEROES or MONSTERS.

... Get There Before Me!: Up to 3 of the targets can each use the 'Normal Move' ability as if it were your movement phase .

... Grab That!: Add 5 to each target's control score for the rest of the battle.

The new Sons of Behemat battletome is up for pre-order on Saturday alongside brand new miniatures. Today, we’re taking a look inside the book to see how their battle traits and other army rules work.

Ask yourself this: how far are you willing to push your luck for big damage? The need to go big or go home has never been more present than the new battletome, as the Sons of Behemat battle traits now centre around a phase-by-phase gamble between small, reliable damage and massive power slams that might get fumbled before they actually happen.

You get to activate an ability in each of the Movement, Charge, and Combat phases – as well as at the end of the turn – that works roughly the same way: 

  1. Select any number of friendly target units.

  2. Roll a D6 and try to roll equal or higher than the number chosen.

  3. If you are successful, choose an effect for each target.

Any target can choose to roll a D3 and, on a 2+, inflict that much mortal damage to a unit they’re in combat with, for some constant chip damage that wears down your opponents over time. Alternatively, each phase has one or more utility abilities that let you pile in further, scoot off the battlefield edge, or move through enemy units and terrain.

If you want real damage, though, you can wind up for the whole turn. All kinds of gargants can build momentum in the Movement phase and get ready in the Charge phase, but while LITTLE units like the new Boss-stompers spend their readiness to gain Strike-first in the Combat phase, BIG units like Mega-Gargants can choose to start prepping the big one.

Unleashing their fury at the end of the turn, a BIG unit that is prepping the big one can choose to grab any number of dice they please and roll them all in one go. If any of them are a 1, the titan stumbles and nothing happens, but otherwise you add every dice result together and inflict that much mortal damage on an unfortunate foe. How lucky do you feel?

BATTLE TRAITS

Once Per Turn (Army), End of Your Turn

THE BIG ONE

The titan slams its foot into the earth, causing a minor seismic rupture. The more anger, momentum and general surliness they have behind them, the more damage they can do…

Declare: Pick any number of friendly Big or Little units to be the targets.

Effect: Roll a dice. If the roll is lower than the number of targets picked, this ability has no effect. Otherwise, pick an effect for each target. The effects must be different unless specified otherwise.

  • Pick an enemy unit in combat with the target and roll a D3. On a 2+, inflict an amount of mortal damage on that enemy unit equal to the roll. You can pick this effect for multiple targets.

  • If the target is prepping the big one, pick an enemy unit in combat with it and roll any number of dice. If any of the rolls are a 1, the target is no longer prepping the big one. Otherwise, add the results together, then inflict an amount of mortal damage on that enemy unit equal to the total.

While this is all going on, your other gargants can be smashing away with smaller amounts of mortal damage, making a fight against the Sons of Behemat a constant race against time. Just remember, if you gamble too much and roll under the number of units you’ve picked each time, the mortal damage train stops with a screech.* 

The battletome also includes new battle formations, heroic traits, and artefacts of power (including the Massive Stuffin’ Sack), as well as the new Lore of Behemat used by the magical Ma Maegran.

There are also a range of new Realm-shaking Rampages. While most inhabitants of the Mortal Realms will be terrified by the thought of a Windmill Walloping or Colossal Slam, we recommend you be very wary of Rancid Flatulence.

REALM-SHAKING RAMPAGES

Once Per Battle (Army), End of Any Turn

RANCID FLATULENCE

Having imbibed a brewery's worth of stolen ale and some questionably sourced meat, this gargant has a very grumbly tummy - with olfactorily obliterative results.

Effect: For the rest of the turn, enemy units have a maximum control score of 1 while they are in combat with this unit.

KEYWORDS: RAMPAGE

Fancy adding a few Mega-Gargants to your army so you can turn toothpick humans into paste with The Big One? The release of Codex: Space Marines isn’t far away, so it’s about time we showed off the book. Sorry, books – there are three different options!

Codex: Space Marines will be available in a regular softback and Special Edition hardback versions, packed to the gills with background lore, artwork, and army rules. The third variant is for true Adeptus Astartes megafans – a glorious Limited Edition.

The front cover is quite special. We’ve done metal details on book covers before – like last year’s Era of Ruin anthology – but this Codex uses a magnetic panel to let you choose your emblem of choice from between the Ultramarines, Raven Guard, Iron Hands, Imperial Fists, Salamanders, or White Scars. You get all six, so you can swap them out whenever you like.

You also get some other incredible goodies, like a metal Crux Terminatus finished in an antique bronze effect so you can show off your service to the Emperor and earn the right to pilot Terminator armour.* To top it off, the Limited Edition Codex includes six art prints and the complete Space Marines Command Pack, so you’ll get the tokens and reference cards you need.

The Special Edition version of the Codex, meanwhile, comes with a wraparound hardback cover showing elements of a Space Marine fortress monastery on the inside. The outer cover is embossed with gold foil details, and the whole thing includes printed page edges and a ribbon page marker so you can keep tabs on your favourite detachment or datasheet.

All three Codexes contain the same content inside, filling a whopping 232 pages with extensive background information on the Space Marines, their organisation, and the units that make up their armies, as well as multiple hobby guides to help you collect and construct the force of your dreams. 

There’s 15 detachments to tailor your army in defence of the Imperium. These are:

The ground is trembling, which can only mean one thing – the Sons of Behemat are on the march, and they have some very large reinforcements joining their latest rampage.

Warhammer Age of Sigmar – Ma Maegran, Chooser of the Mighty

Bestow the blessing of almighty bigness on your chosen Gargants with Ma Maegran, a mystical witch known as the Chooser of the Mighty. Her magical talents are an invaluable tool in any Sons of Behemat army, while her pair of Ancient Ghyrochs gore nearby prey before they can get within arm’s reach of their titanic shepherd.

Warhammer Age of Sigmar – Boss-stompers

Boss-stompers take a more serious and disciplined approach to warfare, by Gargant standards. Their obsession with real fighting skill makes them particularly dangerous foes, adept at clubbing enemies into the dirt.

This box contains three Boss-stompers who can alternately be built as Rock-hurlers – Gargants that prefer to keep their distance and, as their name suggests, hurl rocks. The three Rock-hurlers also make up the new Spearhead army for the Sons of Behemat.

Warhammer Age of Sigmar – Stomper Tribe

Kickstart a force themed around the new Stomper Tribe Army of Renown rules with a boxed set containing a monstrous Warstomper Mega-Gargant and three Mancrusher Gargants. The army is based around a horde of smaller Gargants following in the wake of the Warstomper, gaining powerful boons and a smidge of the warlord’s attention while hanging around his impressive bigness.

The Warstomper can alternatively be built as a Gatebreaker or Kraken-eater Mega-Gargant, while the Mancrushers come with a variety of cosmetic options making them easy to customise. The Stomper Tribe boxed set is only available while stocks last.

Warhammer Age of Sigmar – Brawlers of Behemat

Play out a titanic duel between two raging Mega-Gargants in the Brawlers of Behemat boxed set, featuring easy-to-learn game rules for fast, tactical battles between two massive warriors. You get two complete Mega-Gargants that can each be built as a Warstomper, Gatebreaker, or Kraken-Eater – with rules for all three – as well as a brand new set of ruined Embergard terrain to fight around.

As well as being a fun standalone game, Brawlers of Behemat is also a great way to pick up a pair of Mega-Gargants for your Sons of Behemat army. This boxed set is only available while stocks last.

Warhammer Age of Sigmar – Destruction Battletome: Sons of Behemat

Take your Sons of Behemat into battle with a new battletome packed with background lore, artwork, miniatures galleries, and game rules for your sky-scraping horde. Learn all about the Gargant tribes of the Mortal Realms and their activities in Ghur, before crushing your opposition underfoot with new battle traits, a new Spearhead force, and enough Path to Glory content to send your colossal champions to new heights of infamy.

You’ll be able to get the new Battletome in its regular hardback edition, as well as a pocket-friendly Gamer’s Edition that comes with a set of 33 handy warscroll cards. The Gamer’s Edition is only available while stocks last.

Warhammer Age of Sigmar – Sons of Behemat Warscroll Cards and Dice

Add a set of Warscroll Cards – great for keeping your most important rules handy – and a pack of Sons of Behemat-themed dice to your collection. You get 16 in total, cast in a bloodstained bone-coloured plastic with dark red pips and a big man-crushing foot on the six.

Middle-earth™ Strategy Battle Game – Battlehosts

Start a new army or expand your existing collection with a trio of Battlehost boxes for the Middle-earth Strategy Battle Game. These armies are a great way to try a new faction or learn to play the game, and free downloadable rules right here on the Warhammer Community website will let you play any two Battlehost forces against each other without needing further rulebooks.

Lead your Rohan forces with King Théoden, sneak through the woods with the Legolas and the Mirkwood Battlehost, and smash through your enemies with a Dol Guldur force, commanded by Bolg.

The new House Goliath Underhive Journal is available for pre-order from tomorrow. We’ve asked Rob from the Warhammer Design Studio for some help in getting the most from our muscle-bound gangers.

Rob: House Goliath, also known as the House of Chains, values strength and personal prowess above all. In campaigns they win by surviving hits that would fell others and overwhelming their foes with raw strength.

The Fighters

Having been genetically altered to be the most efficient workers on Necromunda, Goliaths are able to take a beating with their Toughness characteristic defaulting to 4 – higher than any other Clan House gang! Their increased physiology doesn’t stop there; they also gain a +1 Strength bonus during an activation where they Charge (though variant gangs benefit from different quirks of their physiology instead).

The Goliath gang expands on the standard Leader, Champion, Ganger, and Prospect, with Stimmers, Forge-Born, and the Furnace Smelters specialists. Each of these add additional options to your gang enabling them to shore up any weaknesses in their Gang Roster.

Building a Goliath gang follows the same pattern for me as any other gang – I aim for 8-10 Fighters and try to cover the following roles:

  • Close Combat: Each gang needs Fighters who can get up close and personal. With the higher number of attacks generally available in melee as opposed to ranged combat, as well as cover not increasing the target’s Save characteristic, close combat is often more effective at taking enemy models Out of Action. Goliaths have many great options, but they do need to pay greater consideration to protection – many of their most powerful melee weapons have the Unwieldy trait, meaning that your opponent will often get the chance to attack you first. Luckily your Fighters are able to take this punishment with their increased Toughness and I will often prioritise mesh armour for my combat Fighters.

  • Objective Control: This is an area where Goliath gangs can often struggle. With their low Movement and Initiative you will rarely be the first one on an objective. However, the gang is great at clearing objectives of enemies and taking them over! Their increased Strength when performing the Charge action, along with devastating weapons like the ‘Renderizer’, means they will make short work of any who are foolish enough to try and stop them from taking ground.

  • Suppressing Fire: Even though the Goliath are brutally effective at close quarters fighting, it is still important for them to include a variety of ranged combatants. After all, it is no good being able to cave in someone’s head with a spud-jacker if you can’t catch up to them! One of their most effective weapons for this is the stub cannon. With a respectable 18” range and impressive Strength of 5, where it really shines is the Knockback (5+) trait which allows it to clear enemies off objectives, force them off ledges and, if you can get the right angles, knock them out of cover and into the open.

  • Utility: As with all gangs, starting with a respectable number of Prospects is always useful – expendable Fighters who can claim objectives, perform Coup de Grâce actions and advance quickly are too good to pass up. Forge Patchers are especially valuable for the Goliaths – with many of your best combatants taking Wounds from foes with higher Initiative characteristics, being able to restore Wounds to them is a must.

The Weapons

The House of Chains excels at close quarters fighting. Most of their deadliest weapons are shorter ranged than other gangs’ options, but they pack a far bigger punch. For example, the ‘Krumper’ rivet cannon has a modest range of 9”, but hits hard with Str 4, AP -1 and both the Blaze and Rapid Fire traits. If you want to try a really nasty combo, pair this weapon with the Marksman skill, granting the Fighter +1 to Hit for all targets between 3” and 9” away. The ignition cannon is another great example – this weapon (used to ignite the massive smelters within Goliath forges) hits harder than a plasma gun without the risk of hurting the bearer, albeit with a shorter range of 10”.

Gene-smithing

The Goliath were made to be hardy and strong. During their creation by the Escher and Van Saar, many different genetic strands were added and cut, leading to large genetic variety within the clan, not to mention the experimental procedures used to turn others into Unborn. The resulting qualities, both positive and negative, allow for a large amount of customisation in your gang.

There are a wide array of Gene-smithing options available when adding a Goliath to the Gang Roster, ranging from Adaptive Mind, which allows them to treat Secondary skills as Primary skills when generating Advancements, to Redundant Organs, which lowers the chance of a Fighter suffering a bad result on the Lasting Injury table. When selecting Gene-smithing options, bear in mind the intended role for the Fighter and select ones that complement it. Be careful with the negative ones, as although they can seem really good, there will be times you regret them and they can also prevent you taking full advantage of later Advancements.

Campaign Development

As your Prospects gain Advancements, you should start to specialise them towards certain roles based on their Advancement rolls. If you get really lucky and manage to get a 12, it can be really good to pick up one of the skills that are really hard to acquire for a Goliath gang, like Juggernaut or Infiltrate – however, sometimes it is better to pick up a Characteristic increase.

With your Post-cycle actions, the focus should be on developing the Fighters you have. If a Fighter is just one or two XP shy of their next Advancement, Train is a really strong action for them. I always try to have the maximum of five Fighters perform the Work Territory action as this is the most reliable source of credits for your gang. Visit the Trading Post can be a very powerful action if there is certain equipment you have your eye on. Finally, Visit the Doc and Fit Bionics, while situational, are very powerful!

Conclusion

At the end of the day, these are just the tactics that work for me. There are so many different variables in a Necromunda campaign that can completely change the approach to take. Is your campaign full of close combat powerhouses like Corpse Grinder Cults and Malstrain? Prioritise shooting more – heavy stubbers become incredibly powerful weapons, and those with Knockback can really slow the more melee-oriented gangs down while softening them up for your own charge. Keep going up against Van Saar and Ironhead Squat Prospectors? Invest in some smoke grenades and power through their hail of fire in order to crush them at short range.

As with every gang, there’s only one rule that must be followed at all times when playing Necromunda – if you think it will be fun and lead to a cool story, do it!
